yard_exceptions.legislative_history: June 5, 2025 Planning Commission packet (Project 25-056; staff-report cover shows 25-055 — discrepancy preserved) proposed the amendments https://www.murray.utah.gov/DocumentCenter/View/16772/060525-Planning-Commission-Packet?bidId ; Planning Commission recommended approval 6-0 on 2025-06-05 https://www.utah.gov/pmn/files/1295135.pdf ; Committee of the Whole reviewed the proposed ordinance 2025-08-05 https://www.utah.gov/pmn/files/1317619.pdf ; adopted as Ordinance 25-30 (council vote date not captured; ordinance number and current-code history verified in primary code).
yard_exceptions.verbatim_current_text_A: A. The following structures may project into a minimum front or rear yard not more than four feet (4'), and into a minimum side yard not more than two and one-half feet (21/2'): 1. Cornices, eaves, sills, buttresses or other similar architectural features; 2. Fireplace structures and bays; 3. Stairways, balconies, door stoops, fire escapes, awnings, skylights and planting boxes or masonry planters not exceeding twenty four inches (24') in height.
yard_exceptions.verbatim_current_text_B: B. Any permanent roof or canopy attached to the main building which covers a use customarily recognized as an open, outdoor use, such as a patio, patio deck, hot tub, etc., and any uncovered deck attached to the main dwelling may extend into the rear yard no further than one-half the required rear yard setback distances, and into a front yard not more than seven (7) feet, if the following criteria are met: 1. The roof or canopy is not more than one (1) story in height. 2. The roof or canopy is no longer than one-half (1/2) the width of the main dwelling on which it is located. 3. The roof or canopy is entirely open on three (3) sides except for supporting columns and customary architectural features. 4. The columns supporting the roof or canopy are constructed on individual pad footings or similar design, and not on a continuous footing wall that could be used for future expansion of living space. 5. In no instance may the additions encroach to within less than twenty (20) feet of a front or street side yard property line, or to within less than ten (10) feet of a rear property line. (Ord. 25-30 § 2: Ord. 07-30 § 2)
yard_exceptions.scope_note: The same ordinance amended the yard-exception sections of all residential chapters (17.92, 17.96, 17.100, 17.104, 17.108, 17.112, 17.116, 17.120, 17.124, 17.128) per the 2025-06-05 PC motion; verified in current primary text for §17.108.100 (R-1-12) and §17.120.070 (R-M-15, https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/murrayut/latest/murray_ut/0-0-0-12789). These are yard EXCEPTIONS (encroachment allowances), not base yard requirements.

yards.accessory_note: Accessory buildings ≥6 ft to the rear of the main building may have a 1 ft minimum rear yard, provided no accessory building is closer than 10 ft to a dwelling on an adjacent lot, may not encroach upon a public utility easement, must discharge all roof drainage onto the subject property, and must meet city fire/building codes. No accessory building or group in any residential district shall cover more than 25% of the rear yard area.
yards.corner_lot_note: On corner lots the front of the main dwelling maintains the required front-yard setback; using side-yard setbacks in front-yard areas is not allowed. Street-side corner side yard (20 ft) shall not be used for vehicle parking except driveway access to a garage/carport.
yards.driveway_note: Side yard used for access to a detached garage/carport for one dwelling: unobstructed 12 ft paved driveway; for more than one dwelling: unobstructed 25 ft wide driveway.

ratios.multifamily_breakdown: 2 designated stalls per unit plus an additional 0.5 spaces per unit pooled and marked for visitor parking; at least 1 covered stall per unit
ratios.rv_parking_note: Planning Commission may require additional RV parking based on development size, number/size of units, market value, and occupancy mix
ratios.scope_caveat: §17.72.100 states citywide residential ratios. MCCD (chapter 17.170) uses its own Table D (studio 1.0, 1-bed 1.05, 2-bed 1.5, 3+bed 2.5 spaces/unit) — district-specific, NOT chapter 17.72. Do not apply MCCD ratios citywide.

parking_residential_17_72.context: R-M chapters (§§17.116.110, 17.120.110) cross-reference multifamily parking; §17.72.100 is the controlling citywide section.

incentive_density_bonus_17_132.mechanism: To gain bonus density in any multiple-family zone through conditional use permit, the project shall meet criteria under urban design/neighborhood compatibility, energy efficiency, structure design, landscaping, affordable housing, and parking facilities. Portions may be waived/modified by Planning Commission based on project performance; burden of proof rests with applicant.

one_unit_per_acre.affordable_housing: 20% of units affordable to people making 80% or less of median income; units remain affordable for 25 years
one_unit_per_acre.urban_design: 50% of perimeter buildings limited to adjacent structural height; remainder limited to 2 stories; setbacks equal to or greater than surrounding; designed with compatibility to adjacent residential development (height, architecture, landscaping, buffering, traffic, mass)
one_unit_per_acre.landscaping: 30% of site landscaped/recreation; 1 approved tree per 600 sq ft landscaped area; landscaping/berming buffer; high-quality barrier fencing
one_unit_per_acre.structure_design: Variation in detail/form/siting (no repetitious boxlike); 50% of units with outdoor privacy (balconies/patios ≥72 sq ft); laundry facilities on site; mechanical equipment hidden
one_unit_per_acre.parking: 1 covered stall per unit; landscaped islands to break up asphalt; berms to screen/buffer; scatter parking in smaller areas
one_unit_per_acre.building_materials: Quality materials encouraged; no plywood/composition siding; 50% exterior maintenance-free masonry; minimum 240-lb architectural grade asphalt/fiberglass or fire-treated wood shingles

two_units_per_acre.affordable_housing: 20% of units affordable to people making 60% or less of median income; units remain affordable for 25 years
two_units_per_acre.urban_design: 75% of perimeter buildings limited to adjacent structural height; remainder limited to 2 stories; setbacks equal to or greater than surrounding; compatibility with regard to height, architecture, landscaping, traffic, mass
two_units_per_acre.landscaping: 35% of site landscaped/recreation; 1 approved tree per 575 sq ft landscaped area; landscaping/berming buffer; masonry barrier fencing
two_units_per_acre.structure_design: No repetitious/boxlike buildings; no long straight facades; harmonious colors; 75% of units with outdoor privacy (≥72 sq ft); individual washer/dryer hookups; mechanical hidden; 1 special amenity (pool/clubhouse/playground/tennis) for 20+ units
two_units_per_acre.parking: Covered parking design-compatible with dwelling; RV parking 1 stall per 8 units; landscaped islands; berms; scatter parking
two_units_per_acre.building_materials: High quality exterior; no plywood/composition/aluminum/plastic siding (aluminum/plastic soffit/fascia permitted); 75% exterior maintenance-free masonry; minimum 300-lb shingles

three_units_per_acre.affordable_housing: 20% of units affordable to people making 60% or less of median income; units remain affordable for 50 years
three_units_per_acre.urban_design: 100% of perimeter buildings limited to adjacent structural height; visual interest from all angles; setbacks equal to or greater than surrounding for excellent buffering from single-family/commercial; excellent compatibility (height, architecture, landscaping, traffic, mass)
three_units_per_acre.landscaping: 40% of site landscaped/recreation; 1 approved tree per 525 sq ft landscaped area; wide variety of plants/trees; 1 tree per 300 sq ft buffer area
three_units_per_acre.structure_design: Excellent design quality throughout (variation in height, siting, buffering, form, material, texture); 100% of units with outdoor privacy (≥72 sq ft); washer/dryer hookups; maintenance-free fencing; mechanical hidden; 1 amenity for 20+ units, 2 amenities for 30+ units
three_units_per_acre.parking: 1 stall per unit incorporated into main dwelling as garage; RV parking 1 stall per 5 units; landscaped areas; berms; scatter parking
three_units_per_acre.building_materials: Essentially 100% maintenance-free wall material (high-quality brick, natural stone, weather-resistant stucco ≤30%); metal/plastic soffits/fascia permitted; extremely durable roofing (fire-treated wood shakes, clay/concrete tile, slate, or approved high-quality metal)

incentive_density_bonus_17_132.applicability_note: Applies across multiple-family zones (R-M-10 up to 10 u/ac, R-M-15 up to 15 u/ac, R-M-20 up to 20 u/ac, R-M-25 up to 25 u/ac) via conditional use permit. See individual district .040 sections for base densities.
